body.text: RTDs use pure metals or certain alloys that increase in resistance as temperature increases and decrease in resistance as temperature decreases.

body.text: The sheath reaches the temperature of the medium, and the platinum wire heats or cools, producing a proportional change in resistance. A precision measuring device, normally a bridge circuit, is calibrated to give the temperature.

checks.q: What happens to RTD resistance when temperature decreases?
checks.x: The resistance of an RTD varies directly with temperature, so a decrease in temperature decreases resistance.

checks.q: What are RTD elements normally made of?
checks.x: RTD elements are normally constructed of platinum, copper, or nickel.

checks.q: Why is Inconel normally used for the RTD sheath?
checks.x: Inconel is normally used for the sheath because of its inherent corrosion resistance.

checks.q: What does the insulator in an RTD do?
o: Raises the resistance of the wire
Protects the sheath from the process
Prevents a short circuit between the wire and the sheath
checks.x: The insulator prevents a short circuit between the wire and the metal sheath.

body.text: Temperatures may be displayed in a central location, with audible and visual alarms at preset limits. Control functions start or stop equipment, or cause a protective action.
If key temperature sensing instruments fail, some applications use installed spare detectors or dual-element RTDs.
If only the circuitry has failed, an external bridge circuit can be connected to the detector, and readings taken from the calibration curves.
Ambient variations can directly affect the resistance of bridge components and of the thermocouple reference junction.

checks.q: What are the three basic functions of temperature detectors?
checks.x: Temperature detectors provide three basic functions: indication, alarm, and control.

checks.q: If an installed spare is not available, what can measure temperature on accessible equipment?

checks.q: Which two environmental concerns can affect temperature detection instrumentation?
checks.x: Ambient temperature variations and humidity both affect the instrumentation.

body.text: R1 / R3 = R2 / Rx, so Rx = R2R3 / R1

facts.q: How does an RTD respond to a temperature rise?
facts.a: Its resistance increases, because resistance varies directly with temperature.
An RTD with two sensing elements, of which only one is normally connected. The second can be used if the first fails.
A portable thermocouple used to read temperature on accessible equipment.

facts.q: What are the three methods of bridge compensation for ambient temperature?
facts.a: Measuring circuit resistor selection, electronic circuitry design, and three or four wire RTD circuits.

facts.q: How does an open RTD fail compared with a shorted RTD?
facts.a: Open reads very high temperature. Shorted reads very low temperature.

summary.text: The resistance of an RTD varies directly with temperature, and it is constructed of a fine, pure, metallic wire in an insulator and metal sheath.
A thermocouple's measuring junction produces a voltage greater than the reference junction, and the difference is proportional to temperature difference.
Temperature detectors are used for indication, alarm, and control functions.
The bridge circuit is balanced when the sensing ammeter reads zero current.
An open circuit reads very high temperature, and a short circuit reads very low temperature.
